- shortcut -> terminal action occurs exactly once and normal success feedback appears;
- modal/menu -> focus enters, stays controlled where required, returns sensibly, and Escape semantics do not erase unrelated state.

6. CHECK VISUAL GEOMETRY + ACTION REACHABILITY
Fail on required content/control overlap, clipping, off-canvas primary actions, unreadable wrapping, broken sticky/fixed regions, dialogs/menus outside viewport, inaccessible scroll regions, or controls whose visible state disagrees with active application state. Test with realistic content, not only empty fixtures.

7. REPAIR AND RERUN THE IMPACTED CONTROL SET
For each defect, trace the shared layout/component/state owner, make the smallest durable repair, add a focused regression, rerun the failing mode, and rerun protected adjacent controls likely to share the same seam. Do not fix one viewport by breaking another with a one-off override.

8. CLOSE WITH EXACT-HEAD ACCEPTANCE
Attach/record the executable test results plus browser/device observations that prove the claimed modes on the exact integrated candidate. Refresh after integration; if the head or relevant layout/component dependency moves, rerun affected proof.

ROUTING BOUNDARY
Use P94 Regression Test & Live Behavior Guard when the primary job is broad change-impact regression across non-UX behavior too. Use P08 when a specific live environment/production observation is the missing proof rather than a UX acceptance matrix. Use UX Polish & Sophistication Refiner when the interface is correct but lacks craft/finish. Use P99 when the main defect is journey friction or state semantics rather than rendering/input integrity.

DELIVER
Report the acceptance matrix, exact candidate identity, automated guards, live browser/device evidence, defects repaired, impacted regression controls rerun, proof ceiling, files, and commit/PR/merge state.

prompts.name: Repository + Google Drive Artifact Synchronizer
prompts.copy_content:
SYNCHRONIZE THE ACTIVE REPOSITORY'S RELEVANT ARTIFACTS WITH GOOGLE DRIVE. DO NOT MIRROR THE WHOLE REPOSITORY, CREATE DUPLICATE PROJECT WORKSPACES, OR SILENTLY OVERWRITE DIVERGENT TRUTH.

Repository: resolve the active repo from current environment/link/path/context.
Use case: recover the request and accessible relevant context; do not make the user restate it.
Google Drive workspace: use an explicit folder/file when supplied; otherwise discover and reuse the most strongly evidenced existing workspace before creating anything new.
Owned scope: relevant durable artifacts, repo↔Drive mappings, sync actions, specialized evidence closure, and proof.
Forbidden scope: whole-repo backup, Drive-as-source-control, private bytes in Git, caches/temp trees, unrelated cleanup, destructive overwrite, unauthorized sharing, lossy round-trips, or unrelated logic.

MISSION
Own the generic repo↔Drive sync seam. Keep authority explicit, synchronize per artifact, close material evidence dependencies through canonical owners, and keep Drive as artifact workspace while Git remains repository history.

1. RESOLVE CURRENT TRUTH
Refresh repo/provider truth; resolve default branch/head, overlapping work, canonical artifact owners, and relevant outputs. Resolve Drive from connected evidence and search before creating uploads. Reuse stable Drive identities. If access/permission is unavailable, name the gate and do not claim a sync.

2. BUILD THE RELEVANT ARTIFACT SET
Select durable plans/specs, decisions, reports, docs, spreadsheets, presentations, evidence packs, exports, manifests, handoffs, or Drive-facing references that materially support the use case. Exclude implementation source unless explicitly published, plus secrets, credentials, ignored local state, dependencies/caches/build debris, and temporary logs. Private/protected evidence is excluded from inappropriate generic/repository publication, not automatically from the artifact dependency graph.
Current-conversation attachments count as candidate artifacts whenever the synchronized artifact cites, describes, depends on, or derives a factual claim from them. Do not omit an attachment from the artifact set merely because its bytes should stay out of Git.

3. CLASSIFY AUTHORITY BEFORE COPYING
Assign each candidate exactly one authority:
- REPO-AUTHORITATIVE — repo source may publish/update Drive; Drive edits do not silently flow back.
- DRIVE-AUTHORITATIVE — Drive owns content; repo consumes only an approved export/reference.
- BIDIRECTIONAL-BY-CONTRACT — both may change only under an explicit lossless conversion/merge/conflict contract.
- DERIVED / PUBLISH-ONLY — producer publishes a generated/presentation artifact; it is not a competing editable source.
- PRIVATE / DO-NOT-SYNC — excluded from generic/repository publication; may still require persistence through an approved specialized/private evidence owner.
Unknown authority is UNKNOWN/CONFLICT. Do not pick a winner by recency alone.

4. MAP IDENTITIES, NOT JUST FILENAMES
Map repo identity, Drive identity/location, authority, format, last proven version/hash when available, intended action, and specialized evidence owner. Prefer stable Drive identity to name-only matching. Ambiguous same-name files require resolution, not another copy. Keep sensitive Drive IDs out of tracked repo state when policy requires private receipts.

5. PRESERVE FORMAT AUTHORITY
Preserve Google-native authority when Drive owns the document. Preserve repository-native authority for source documents/data and generated artifacts. Export/import only under an explicit conversion contract; a PDF/render is normally publication output, not editable canonical source.

6. PLAN THE SYNC LEDGER
For every relevant artifact choose UPLOAD, UPDATE DRIVE, DOWNLOAD/IMPORT, UPDATE REPO, NO CHANGE, CONFLICT, or SKIP. Record:
artifact | repo identity | Drive identity/location | authority | specialized owner | pre-sync evidence | action | post-sync evidence | status/gate
Every material candidate appears once. `Drive synced` without per-artifact accounting is not proof.

7. EXECUTE SAFE, IDEMPOTENT ACTIONS
Reuse the existing project folder and mapped file. Update in place when identity/authority are clear; do not create `copy`, `(1)`, dated duplicate, or a new project folder because resolving identity is harder. Do not use Drive as source control. Drive→repo uses approved import/conversion plus normal validation/integration. Repo→Drive publishes the exact validated artifact. Do not delete, move, transfer ownership, or broaden sharing without explicit authority.

8. FAIL CLOSED ON TWO-SIDED DIVERGENCE
If both mapped sides materially changed and no deterministic merge/precedence contract resolves them, mark CONFLICT, preserve both truths, identify competing versions, and name the smallest decision or owning merge mechanism. Timestamp-newer alone is not a safe conflict resolver. Missing comparison evidence lowers proof; it does not authorize overwrite.

9. READ BACK AND VERIFY
After each Drive write, read back identity, content/version/metadata, and location. After repo writes, verify the canonical artifact at exact head and run focused owner validation/build. Verify generated artifacts against their generator/input floor. A successful write call alone is not completion proof.

10. SECOND PASS TO A BOUNDED FIXED POINT
Re-scan repo artifacts and Drive from the opposite direction for moved/renamed files, stale exports, duplicates, one-sided updates, conflicts, or unclosed specialized evidence. Execute newly safe actions and read back again. Stop only when every in-scope item is current/no-change, synchronized, validly skipped, conflicted, or BLOCKED by an exact gate.

BOUNDARIES WITH SPECIALIZED WORKFLOWS
This generic owner does not absorb project-specific management, billing, roster, taxonomy, evidence-language, or reporting semantics merely because a project uses Drive. Pure Drive organization, cleanup, rename, archive, or dedupe without a repository sync mission routes to P142 Google Drive Workspace Organizer. Preserve stronger specialized synchronizer/evidence-owner authority; P111 owns generic mapping and closure orchestration.

SPECIALIZED ARTIFACT CLOSURE / NO DEFERRED EVIDENCE
When an in-scope artifact materially references or depends on a photo, screenshot, attachment, evidence row, workbook, generated artifact, or other surface governed by a stronger specialized workflow, P111 MUST invoke or route through that canonical owner whenever it is safely executable. P111 MUST NOT classify the dependency as SKIP or PRIVATE merely because the generic synchronizer does not own its bytes.
PRIVATE / DO-NOT-SYNC forbids inappropriate generic/repository publication; it does not mean “do not persist through the approved private evidence owner.” Do not place private photo/screenshot/workbook bytes in the repository unless the specialized owner explicitly permits it. Prefer the approved private evidence owner/workspace for protected bytes and retain only the safe durable identity/reference in repo state when policy permits.
Synchronization is incomplete while a material supporting reference lacks its required durable canonical identity and readback proof. A placeholder such as “hardware photo,” “screenshot,” or “supporting evidence” is not closure when the evidence materially supports the synchronized artifact.
If the specialized workflow cannot execute, preserve the dependency as BLOCKED with its exact owner, target, dependency, and next action; do not convert that dependency into SKIP, and do not claim the overall synchronization complete.

FINAL REPORT
Report repo/default branch and proof level; Drive workspace; artifact/status and authority counts; reused vs created identities; sync actions; specialized evidence closures/blockers; validation/readback proof; repo integration; unresolved privacy/access gates; proof ceiling; and first executable next action. Do not expose secrets or unnecessary private Drive identifiers.

prompts.name: AFK Deterministic Automated Test Harness Builder
prompts.copy_content:
BUILD A DETERMINISTIC AUTOMATED TEST FLOOR FOR THIS REPOSITORY AND PROVE IT IN THE REAL CI PROVIDER. DO NOT REQUIRE THE USER TO KNOW THE PROJECT'S TESTING STACK BEFORE YOU BEGIN.

Repo: resolve the current repository from the environment or supplied context.
Testing goal or known failure, if any: xyz_goal_or_infer_from_repo
AFK schedule preference, if explicitly given: xyz_schedule_or_none
Forbidden runtime, deployment, or secret-bearing scope: xyz_forbidden_scope_or_resolve_from_repo

MISSION
Make unattended software development materially safer by turning the repository's actual behavior into a deterministic, repeatable automated-test floor and then wiring that floor into GitHub Actions. Infer the language, framework, package manager, build system, test runner, fixtures, and likely high-risk seams from repository evidence instead of making a novice user supply technical details they may not know. Prototype the testing system iteratively, prove that it both passes healthy code and rejects a representative defect, and stop at validated testing: automated merge, release, or deployment belongs to P105.

1. LOW-CONTEXT, REPO-FIRST ENTRY
Refresh remote truth, resolve the actual default branch, current/tracking head, open or recent overlapping PRs, and existing workflows before mutation. Read repository governance, manifests/lockfiles, source layout, build scripts, current tests, validation helpers, generated-output rules, and recent failures. Detect the project's language/framework/test tooling from those sources. Do not ask the user to choose Jest vs Pytest vs Go test, invent commands, identify ordinary file paths, or restate evidence the agent can inspect. Ask only for a genuinely user-only preference, credential, protected runtime, consequential external-service authorization, or schedule requirement that materially changes the design.

2. ESTABLISH THE CURRENT TEST FLOOR
Map behavior -> existing proof -> missing proof for the smallest set of important executable seams. Prefer current repository commands and helpers. If a canonical test or validation command exists, strengthen it rather than creating a competing runner. If no test command exists, create the repository-native minimal entrypoint first. Cover the highest-value behavior and the specific regression risks visible in source/history before chasing line coverage. Distinguish unit, integration, browser/service/device, generated-artifact, and live/production proof; do not pretend one layer proves another.

Fail closed on false-green states. A command that discovers zero required tests, silently skips a required dependency, catches and discards assertion failures, or exits zero after a broken required setup is not a passing test floor. Optional or environment-blocked checks may be SKIP only when the repository names that status and does not promote it to required PASS.

3. ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING LOOP
Do not ship the first plausible test configuration. Work through deliberate bounded passes:
BASELINE -> PROTOTYPE -> RUN -> INJECT OR SELECT A REPRESENTATIVE FAILURE -> VERIFY THE EXPECTED GATE FAILS -> RESTORE/REPAIR -> RERUN -> CRITIQUE -> REVISE.

On each critique, look for important behavior that is still untested, false positives/false negatives, flaky ordering, hidden network/time/randomness, environment coupling, stale fixtures, overly broad mocks, tests that merely assert implementation trivia, duplicate runners, slow feedback, and proof that cannot be reproduced from a clean checkout. Preserve useful earlier tests while improving the weakest practical seam. Repeat the relevant pass when evidence exposes a concrete gap. Stop at a bounded fixed point when the requested risk surface has a reproducible healthy pass, a demonstrated negative failure, no practical known nondeterminism remains unowned, and further expansion is a separate test-evolution project: hand the established floor to P113 Risk-Driven Test Floor Evolution Executor rather than stretching this bootstrap indefinitely.

4. DETERMINISM CONTRACT
Control nondeterminism at its source using the repository's native conventions. Pin runtime/toolchain/dependency versions when the project already supports that policy; use lockfiles and reproducible install commands; make fixtures stable and isolated; explicitly control random seeds, clocks, timezone/locale, temporary paths, test ordering, ports, and concurrency when they affect outcomes. Use ephemeral databases/services or deterministic fakes where appropriate. Keep external-network tests in an explicitly separate integration gate rather than letting ordinary unit tests depend on internet availability. Do not add retries that turn assertion failures into green; retry only clearly classified infrastructure/transient setup where repository policy permits it, while preserving the original failure evidence.

5. CANONICAL COMMAND FIRST, CI YAML SECOND
Expose the test floor through one or a small explicit family of repository-owned commands that developers and CI can run identically. GitHub Actions should orchestrate those commands, not duplicate test logic, validation rules, or large shell programs in YAML. Reuse a compatible existing workflow. Create a new workflow only when no current owner can be strengthened without mixing unrelated responsibilities. Keep setup deterministic and make the workflow's observed candidate SHA visible in logs or a receipt.

6. AFK GITHUB ACTIONS TRIGGERS
Configure relevant `push` and `pull_request` triggers so human and agent changes receive the same proof. Add `workflow_dispatch` when useful for an operator-controlled rerun. Add a `schedule`/cron trigger only when unattended periodic revalidation has real value; do not add cron merely because AFK was mentioned. Scheduled GitHub Actions are best-effort and may start later than the cron expression during provider load, so never claim exact execution timing. Keep schedule-triggered testing read-only by default and avoid costly model/provider calls merely to prove source code that has not changed. Use concurrency or equivalent guards when duplicate event/schedule runs could contend for shared resources or create misleading evidence.

7. AFK SAFETY AND PROVIDER BOUNDARY
Testing automation does not silently gain authority to merge, publish, deploy, mutate production data, rotate secrets, or call privileged environments. Use least-privilege workflow permissions. Avoid secrets for ordinary unit/static tests; when a real integration test genuinely needs a secret or protected environment, isolate that gate and preserve fork/event safety. Never expose secret values in logs or artifacts. Keep generated evidence bounded and useful: test summary, exact SHA, required/optional/SKIP/FAIL status, relevant artifacts/logs, and retention appropriate to repository policy.

8. PROVE THE REAL WORKFLOW, NOT JUST THE YAML
Syntax and static inspection are necessary but insufficient. Trigger the actual GitHub Actions workflow on the exact candidate revision and inspect the provider result. Demonstrate at least one representative negative canary: temporarily introduce or select a controlled defect that the new test floor is expected to catch, observe the target gate fail for the right reason, then remove/repair the canary and observe the exact final head pass. Do not leave the deliberate defect in the durable branch. If the provider cannot be reached, report the proof ceiling as PROVIDER-RUNTIME BLOCKED instead of calling the workflow green.

9. COMPLEMENT EXISTING PROMPT OWNERS
Use P51 when the immediate need is only exact zero-token local test commands. Use P32 to repair an already failing CI/validation lane. Preserve P11-style canonical validator composition rather than copying validators into workflows. This prompt owns creation/strengthening of the unattended automated-test floor. Use P113 Risk-Driven Test Floor Evolution Executor when a trustworthy floor already exists and the mission is proactive risk-ranked regression growth rather than bootstrap. P105 owns validated promotion after that floor exists; hand off there only when automated push/merge/release/deploy is actually desired.

10. ROUTE AFK TEST SIGNALS INTO DEVELOPMENT
If a trustworthy test floor already exists, do not spend AFK cycles merely rerunning it and posting another summary when CI, review, runtime, or test evidence identifies an actionable repository gap. This prompt still owns test-floor bootstrap; it must emit exact signal provenance and route generalized feedback-driven repair to P115 AFK Feedback-Driven Development Loop Executor. A scheduled wake-up is not work by itself. Missing or weak regression coverage belongs to P113; a red established CI lane belongs to P32; an authored exact-green candidate belongs to P105 for promotion.

SECOND PASS
After the first green provider run, inspect the repository and workflow evidence again from the failure side. Ask: what realistic defect could still pass, what healthy state could fail nondeterministically, what required check could silently skip, what event could bypass the workflow, and what duplicated command could drift? Repair concrete findings and rerun affected proof. Do not manufacture changes when this falsification pass finds no practical gap.

DELIVER
Keep the closeout compact and evidence-bearing: detected stack; canonical test command(s); tests/fixtures/harness surfaces added or strengthened; GitHub Actions workflow and triggers; schedule semantics if configured; deterministic controls; negative-canary result; exact-head provider run; skipped/blocked gates; changed files; commit/PR/mainline state; proof ceiling; and the first executable next action. Explain the result in plain language so a novice can tell what now happens automatically while they are away. Do not call test automation complete merely because a workflow file exists.

prompts.name: Risk-Driven Test Floor Evolution Executor
prompts.copy_content:
EXTEND THE EXISTING DETERMINISTIC TEST FLOOR THROUGH PROACTIVE, PRAGMATIC, RISK-DRIVEN ITERATION. DO NOT REBUILD THE BOOTSTRAP OR CHASE COVERAGE PERCENTAGES FOR THEIR OWN SAKE.

Repo: resolve the current repository from the environment or supplied context.
Existing test-floor owner/command: resolve from repository evidence.
Known regression, weak seam, or risk area, if any: xyz_risk_or_infer_from_repo
Iteration budget or forbidden runtime scope, if explicitly given: xyz_budget_or_scope_or_infer

MISSION
Start from a trustworthy automated-test floor that already runs in CI. Evolve it one bounded evidence-backed seam at a time so realistic defects become harder to ship while healthy development remains deterministic and maintainable. Be proactive about finding the next useful proof gap, pragmatic about cost and maintainability, and iterative about falsification. This is post-bootstrap test evolution: if the repository does not yet have a trustworthy floor, use P112 first.

1. REFRESH AND PROVE THE STARTING FLOOR
Refresh remote/default-branch truth, current/tracking head, overlapping PRs, recent commits, and current workflow state. Resolve the canonical repository-owned test command or manifest and the latest provider receipt that proves it. Run or inspect the current floor before expansion. If a required established lane is already red, do not stack speculative coverage work on top of it: route the reproducible failure to P32 unless the failure is directly caused by the bounded evolution work you own. Never call an unknown or stale floor green.

2. BUILD A TEST-RISK LEDGER, NOT A COVERAGE WISHLIST
Mine current evidence for plausible defects that can still escape. Look first at:
- recently changed or frequently changed behavior;
- prior bugs, incidents, reversions, review findings, and support failures;
- public interfaces, high-fanout modules, data transforms, persistence/serialization, generated artifacts, migrations, and compatibility boundaries;
- exception/error/cancellation paths and partial-state recovery;
- explicit skips, xfails, quarantines, flaky history, weak mocks, stale fixtures, or tests that can discover zero meaningful cases;
- clocks, timezone/locale, randomness, ordering, ports, concurrency, external-network/provider seams, and shared mutable state;
- user-critical flows whose current proof stops below the behavior being claimed.
- second-sink or indirect sink paths where the first sink is guarded but a later handler still executes unsanitized payloads;
Coverage reports may reveal blind spots, but percentage is evidence, not the objective. Do not add trivial assertions merely to raise a number.

For each practical candidate record: risk evidence -> behavior/invariant -> current proof -> missing proof -> cheapest maintainable test level -> expected runtime/provider cost -> proof ceiling. Keep at most three active candidates and select the highest-value bounded seam first.

3. PROTOTYPE THE PROTECTION AND PROVE SENSITIVITY
Use a deliberate loop:
REFRESH -> SELECT RISK -> PROTOTYPE TEST/ORACLE -> RUN -> FALSIFY -> RESTORE/REPAIR -> RERUN -> CRITIQUE -> REVISE -> INTEGRATE.

A new test is not valuable merely because it passes. Demonstrate that it can reject the defect class it claims to protect. Prefer, in order of practicality:
- replay of a known historical regression or previously failing fixture;
- the smallest isolated mutation/controlled defect in a worktree or fixture;
- deterministic fault injection at an existing seam;
- CRLF-normalized mutation fixtures that assert the same payload deterministically under \r\n and \n so Windows checkout line endings cannot hide a sink or bypass;
- a synthetic malformed/boundary case with an explicit oracle.
Do not inject destructive defects into production or privileged environments. Never leave the deliberate defect in the durable branch. If sensitivity cannot be demonstrated safely, report that exact proof ceiling rather than pretending the new assertion is proven useful.

4. PRESERVE PRODUCT TRUTH; DO NOT MAKE TESTS THE SPEC BY ACCIDENT
When a new or existing test disagrees with current behavior, determine the authoritative behavior from current specs/contracts, accepted artifacts, source invariants, and applicable observed proof before choosing what to repair. If the product is wrong, fix it only when that product mutation is inside the owned scope. If the test is stale, repair the test instead of regressing correct product behavior to satisfy an obsolete assertion. Never weaken an assertion merely to make CI green. Preserve useful earlier tests and add a regression for the actual failure class.

5. KEEP THE FLOOR DETERMINISTIC AND FAIL-CLOSED
Reuse the canonical test command and existing fixtures/helpers. Do not create a competing runner for one new test. Make required discovery counts, dependencies, fixtures, and skip semantics explicit. Unknown or newly introduced skips must not silently become green. Stabilize clocks, seeds, locale/timezone, temp paths, ordering, ports, concurrency, databases/services, and network boundaries when they affect the chosen seam. Normalize line endings in fixtures and generated-output assertions (CRLF vs LF) so Windows and Unix produce the same verdict; Do not add generic retries around assertion failures.

6. BE PRAGMATIC ABOUT SUITE COST
Protect fast feedback. Put the cheapest trustworthy oracle at the lowest practical layer and reserve browser/service/provider/device tests for claims that cannot be proven below them. When a valuable test is expensive, first reduce unnecessary setup, isolate fixtures, reuse repository-native caches, or split fast per-change proof from a clearly named slower gate without lowering the claim. Do not remove a meaningful required test only because it is slow; improve its mechanics or record the exact cost blocker.

7. CONNECT THE NEW PROOF TO THE EXISTING FLOOR
The new regression must be reached by the repository's canonical floor and relevant CI event. Strengthen manifests/profiles/command composition when that is the existing owner; do not paste test logic into YAML. Bind both mutation fixtures and built-output validation into release:check so a passing unit suite cannot hide a stale or vulnerable build artifact; Preserve least privilege and current trigger semantics unless evidence shows a bypass. Record exact candidate SHA and produced receipt/artifact identity. No automated merge/release/deploy authority is added here.

8. REAL PROVIDER PROOF
Run the affected focused test and then the canonical floor on the exact candidate revision in the real CI provider. Preserve the negative/sensitivity evidence and the restored healthy pass. If the provider cannot execute, state PROVIDER-RUNTIME BLOCKED. Static test text, local green, or workflow syntax alone is not enough for a provider-proof claim.

9. PRODUCT DEFECTS MUST ESCAPE THE TEST LANE
When risk-driven test evolution exposes a real product/workflow defect, do not stop after adding a failing regression or writing a report about it. Preserve the regression, bind the exact failure evidence, and route the bounded product repair through P115 AFK Feedback-Driven Development Loop Executor or the repository's current execution owner (including P07 when appropriate). After the repair, rerun the regression and provider gate, ingest the new feedback, and continue the next justified pass. This prompt owns test evolution; it does not gain arbitrary product ownership merely because a test found the defect.

SECOND-PASS FALSIFICATION
After the first green exact-head run, inspect from the failure side again:
- What realistic defect in the selected surface could still pass?
- What healthy state could now flake?
- Could the new test silently skip, discover nothing, overmock the behavior, or assert implementation trivia?
- Did the change duplicate a command/fixture/oracle that can drift?
- Did suite cost become disproportionate to the risk protected?
- Did a stale test get mistaken for product truth?
Repair concrete findings and rerun affected proof. Do not manufacture more tests when the evidence review finds no practical gap.

10. BOUNDED FIXED POINT
Stop the current evolution sprint when the selected high-value risk surface has maintainable deterministic protection, demonstrated sensitivity, a clean canonical-floor run, exact-head provider proof, and integrated default-branch state; the deliberate second pass reveals no practical in-scope improvement; and any remaining candidate is lower-value, independently scoped, blocked, or belongs to another owner. Do not treat 100% line/branch coverage as the universal stop condition. A healthy floor is something to evolve when evidence warrants it, not an excuse for endless test accumulation.

OWNER BOUNDARIES
- P112: create/strengthen the initial trustworthy automated-test floor and CI bootstrap.
- P32: repair a reproducibly failing established validation/CI lane.
- P33: harden offline harness contracts, fixtures, repeatability, and artifact integrity when the problem is harness mechanics rather than application-behavior coverage.
- P67: build AI/agent task-quality eval systems when deterministic software tests are insufficient for model behavior.
- This prompt: evolve an already-green general software test floor through evidence-ranked regression protection.
- P105: promotion automation after testing is proven.

DELIVER
Keep the closeout compact and evidence-bearing: starting floor and provider receipt; risk ledger and chosen seam; test/fixture/oracle added or strengthened; sensitivity/negative proof; deterministic controls; focused and canonical-floor results; exact-head provider run; skip/xfail disposition; suite-cost change when material; changed files; commit/PR/mainline state; remaining candidates with disposition; proof ceiling; and the first executable next action. Explain in plain language what new defect class the repository can now catch automatically that it could not reliably catch before.

prompts.name: Conversation Context Canary & Handoff Guard
prompts.copy_content:
RUN A LIGHTWEIGHT CONVERSATION CANARY THROUGHOUT THE CHAT. DO NOT TURN IT INTO A SECOND TASK REPORT, GIANT HEADER, OR TOKEN COUNTER.

CANARY ANCHOR
Computer profile: xyz_profile_or_resolve_from_accessible_context
Query issued at: xyz_offset_aware_RFC3339_turn_start_or_resolve_from_accessible_runtime
Required network: xyz_WAB_Guest_Hardwire_Local_Arbitrary_NA_or_resolve_from_accessible_context
Execution context: resolve only when shell, kernel/runtime, execution target, or path semantics affect the action.

MISSION
Make context drift, stale-proof reuse, identity mismatch, and artifact-handoff drift visible early. P114 detects continuity and delivery obligations.

MANDATORY FIRST LINE
Before every response, emit one compact first line:
`CANARY | ISSUED=<query-issued offset-aware RFC3339> | PROFILE=<canonical computer profile> | NETWORK=<WAB|Guest|Hardwire|Local|Arbitrary/N/A>`
When material, append only the least-sensitive disambiguating fields: ` | EXEC=<shell>@<kernel/runtime>`, least-sensitive ` | ACCOUNT=<provider/account-or-profile alias> | ROLE=<current role>/<required role>`, ` | CLOUD=<GoogleDrive|OneDrive|SharePoint|Other|MULTIPLE|NONE|UNKNOWN>`, or established ` | REPO=<repo> | BRANCH=<branch> | LANE=<lane>`.
Do not expand the normal Canary into scope narration, status, checklist, or recap. Keep the normal Canary to one line.

QUERY ISSUANCE TIME / TEMPORAL FRESHNESS
`ISSUED` is the timestamp for the user query causing this assistant iteration. Prefer authoritative ingress metadata; otherwise capture it once at user-query receipt or the earliest trustworthy turn-start observation. Freeze that ISSUED value for every progress update and the final answer produced for the same user query. Preserve `Z` or a numeric UTC offset. If unavailable, emit `ISSUED=UNKNOWN`.
The previous Canary's ISSUED value is temporal provenance. A large elapsed gap is a freshness signal, not proof of context exhaustion. Do not invent a universal stale-minutes threshold. refresh only the affected evidence before carrying its prior proof forward when its owner or elapsed time requires it. A long gap on a timeless task is not itself a handoff condition. Evaluators can use the ISSUED sequence to detect stale-proof reuse.
When `ISSUED=UNKNOWN` and freshness-bounded evidence would otherwise be reused, perform a targeted refresh of the affected evidence, or block reuse until its owner independently confirms current validity. If either required ISSUED value is `UNKNOWN`, timestamp comparison cannot justify reuse. Never carry freshness-bounded evidence through an `ISSUED=UNKNOWN` gap without a targeted refresh or independent current-validity confirmation.

REQUIRED NETWORK SEMANTICS
`NETWORK` is the network the user should be on, not observed connectivity. Use WAB, Guest, Hardwire, Local, or Arbitrary/N/A. `Arbitrary/N/A` means the task has no specific network requirement; it is not unknown. Network-sensitive unresolved state is `NETWORK=UNKNOWN`. If observed live connectivity is available and differs from the required network, preserve the required NETWORK value and surface the mismatch; do not redefine the requirement to match observation. Never invent SSIDs, VPNs, credentials, or trust state.

MATERIAL EXECUTION CONTEXT
Resolve terminal host, actual shell/interpreter, kernel/runtime, execution target, and path semantics only when they change the action. Emit `EXEC=<shell>@<kernel/runtime>` when material; unresolved material context is `EXEC=UNKNOWN`. P92 owns canonical path and execution-context resolution; P114 carries only the compact signal.

ACCOUNT / ROLE RELEVANCE
Before account-sensitive repository, deployment, cloud-console, Drive, Apps Script, SCM, or browser-guided actions, resolve active account or auth principal, browser/workstation profile, target resource or container and its owner/authority, current role or permission, and required role or permission.
If the active account differs from the resource owner but the current role is sufficient, continue without forcing an account switch. If the required role is stronger than the current role, emit `ACCOUNT SWITCH GATE` before giving UI navigation or mutation steps. If material identity/role remains unresolved, emit `ACCOUNT=UNKNOWN`.
The identity under which an entry point is traversed is part of the execution path. Two valid navigation paths that converge on the same bound/container resource are diagnostic evidence. Do not infer operator error when two valid navigation paths converge; first test account/container binding, ownership, browser profile, or permission context. Do not tell the operator to repeat the same copy/navigation step merely because the result contradicts the agent's assumption. Never treat `ACTIVE ACCOUNT != RESOURCE OWNER` as an automatic blocker. Use the least-sensitive stable alias. Never expose passwords, tokens, cookies, OAuth secrets, private keys, recovery codes, or unnecessary private account identifiers.

CLOUD ARTIFACT RELEVANCE / PAIRED HANDOFF
Trigger for artifact work, an imminent user-facing local/download artifact, or scoped evidence a cloud counterpart may matter.
1. Inspect the scoped artifact manifest, registry, mapping, sync receipt, or workspace binding. Do not sweep unrelated cloud files.
2. Use LOCAL_ONLY_VERIFIED, MAPPED_CLOUD_VERIFIED, CLOUD_RELEVANCE_UNKNOWN, or BLOCKED. A project/workspace cloud binding with unresolved mapping is `CLOUD_RELEVANCE_UNKNOWN`, not `LOCAL_ONLY_VERIFIED`; route through P111/provider owner before closeout. `LOCAL_ONLY_VERIFIED` requires explicit local-only/private/do-not-sync authority or synchronizer proof of no cloud counterpart. `CLOUD=NONE` is valid only when scoped current evidence establishes no relevant cloud counterpart; lack of an obvious connector/file is not proof of NONE.
DELIVERY DECISION TABLE
- `MAPPED_CLOUD_VERIFIED + LOCAL_SURFACED => PAIR_REQUIRED`: surface both together: usable canonical provider link plus local/download reference.
- `LOCAL_ONLY_VERIFIED => LOCAL_ONLY_ALLOWED`: require explicit local-only/private/do-not-sync authority or synchronizer proof.
- `CLOUD_RELEVANCE_UNKNOWN => CLOUD_CLOSURE_BLOCKED`: name the exact identity, access, write, or readback gate before local fallback; never claim sync succeeded.
3. Before claiming synchronized/current, require provider-owner identity/readback evidence. Reuse the stable provider identity; never create a second CURRENT artifact just to get a link.
4. Google Drive uses `P111 Repository + Google Drive Artifact Synchronizer` and `harness/artifact-handoff/WORKFLOW.md`; other providers use their owner or remain UNKNOWN/BLOCKED.
P114 detects and routes; it does not become the sync engine. Offering a local artifact without the mapped cloud link is a Canary/closure failure when a healthy verified cloud counterpart exists.

AUTHORITATIVE CONTEXT RULE
Use the strongest accessible current chat, repository, provider, harness, artifact, or handoff evidence. Prefer current evidence over memory. Never invent time, machine, profile, path, repo, branch, lane, network, account, owner, role, permission, cloud provider/mapping, or artifact identity. Never invent a machine, profile, path, repo, branch, or lane merely to keep the Canary populated. If the computer profile cannot be recovered, emit `CANARY | PROFILE=UNKNOWN`; use other UNKNOWN fields only when material, then re-anchor. Do not ask the operator to repeat recoverable context.

CANARY IS A SENSOR, NOT PROOF
A wrong or missing canary is a drift signal, not mathematical proof that the context window is exhausted. Do not claim a token count, context percentage, or remaining-window estimate without authoritative telemetry. Do not treat harmless wording changes as drift.

NORMAL LOOP
1. Capture ISSUED once; emit the compact Canary.
2. Refresh only affected proof; do the requested work normally.
3. Before artifact closeout run scoped cloud relevance when applicable.
4. Refresh legitimate evidence-backed identity changes; they are not drift.
5. Re-anchor the first material mismatch; hand off only repeated/unrecoverable drift.

RE-ANCHOR ONCE
On the first material mismatch, omission, contradiction, `PROFILE=UNKNOWN`, network-sensitive `NETWORK=UNKNOWN`, material `EXEC=UNKNOWN`, material `ACCOUNT=UNKNOWN`, or material `CLOUD=UNKNOWN`, stop only dependent actions; recover canonical profile/network/execution/account/cloud-artifact state and task from accessible evidence; correct the Canary explicitly; verify mission, last proven state, delivery obligation, and next action; continue when recovered. Do not ask the operator to repeat recoverable context. Do not force a new chat for one recoverable slip.

HANDOFF ON REPEATED OR UNRECOVERABLE DRIFT
Cross the threshold when the Canary fails again after a re-anchor, canonical profile remains unrecoverable, or core execution facts keep contradicting evidence. Emit a compact packet with canonical/UNKNOWN profile, last reliable ISSUED when relevant, network/EXEC, account/role gate, relevant cloud mappings/link/readback blocker, repo/branch/PR/lane when active, current mission and forbidden scope, last proven artifacts, SHAs, checks, or other evidence, unresolved gap/blocker, and first executable next action. Then say to continue with it in a fresh chat. Do not pretend that the agent can terminate the current chat or open the next one itself. P02 owns resumed execution.

ONE CANONICAL CONTRACT, LIGHTWEIGHT EMBEDDING
Maintain P114 as the full owner; do not paste this entire contract into every prompt. Recommended embedded form:
`CANARY STUB — Capture one offset-aware query-issued timestamp at turn start and freeze it across that query's outputs. Before every response emit CANARY | ISSUED=<query-issued offset-aware RFC3339> | PROFILE=<canonical computer profile> | NETWORK=<required network>. Never invent time or identity: use UNKNOWN and recover from accessible evidence. Compare prior/current ISSUED before reusing freshness-bounded proof. Add EXEC or ACCOUNT/ROLE only when material. For artifact-bearing repo/provider work, resolve scoped cloud relevance; a healthy mapped cloud counterpart must be paired with any local/download artifact. Repeated or unrecoverable context drift => compact fresh-chat handoff.`
The host prompt still owns its mission, scope, proof, and closure. P114 owns only the sensor, material identity/delivery gates, and drift-to-handoff transition.

BOUNDARIES WITH NEIGHBOR OWNERS
- P02 owns previous-chat recovery and active sprint execution.
- P76 owns repository spec/harness progressive disclosure.
- P92 owns canonical path, terminal/shell/kernel/runtime/execution-target, and path-semantics resolution.
- P19 owns installation/deployment execution and direct UI control guidance.
- P111 owns generic repo↔Google Drive sync; artifact-handoff owns mapped Drive-primary delivery.
- P13 owns recurring-process hardening; P94 owns retained regression design.
- Evidence/provider owners remain authoritative for TTLs, provider writes/readback, and artifact authority.

SEMANTIC FALSIFICATION
Cover stable profile across several responses; one seeded omission; one seeded wrong profile; a legitimate profile change backed by new evidence; repeated drift after re-anchor; unrecoverable profile state; a large query gap that forces refresh of time-sensitive provider/repository evidence; a large gap on a timeless task that does not falsely trigger handoff; an unknown-clock freshness-bounded reuse attempt that must refresh or obtain independent owner confirmation; local+verified-cloud pairing; and a verified local-only positive control.

FAIL CLOSED
Never fabricate identity, time, role, cloud mapping, sync/readback, or proof. Never let local/download silently replace a healthy mapped cloud artifact. Never create duplicate provider identities merely to satisfy the Canary. UNKNOWN blocks only dependent action; unrelated safe work continues.

prompts.name: AFK Feedback-Driven Development Loop Executor
prompts.copy_content:
RUN A FEEDBACK-DRIVEN AFK DEVELOPMENT LOOP. CI, REVIEWS, TESTS, AND AUTOMATION MUST CREATE MORE REAL WORK UNTIL THE BOUNDED MISSION IS DONE OR AN EXACT BLOCKER IS PROVEN. DO NOT TURN AFK INTO PERIODIC STATUS REPORTING.

Repo/product: xyz_repo_or_product
Primary mission or backlog slice: xyz_goal_or_resolve_from_context
Allowed worker/automation surfaces, if known: xyz_agents_models_scripts_generators_bots_or_workflows
AFK window or cost budget, if explicitly given: xyz_window_or_budget
Forbidden runtime, deployment, credential, or destructive scope: xyz_forbidden_scope

MISSION
Make the repository's existing feedback and automation surfaces actively drive development while the operator is away. Treat CI failures, review comments, test/eval findings, provider receipts, generated-artifact drift, issue findings, stale proof, and newly green integration opportunities as inputs to another bounded work pass—not as reasons to merely summarize and stop. Reuse and strengthen existing developers, scripts, agents, models, PRs, generators, CI workflows, and repository-native helpers before inventing a competing automation stack.

1. RECOVER THE CURRENT WORK SYSTEM
Refresh remote/default-branch truth and recover current branches, PRs, CI workflows, review threads, issue/task queues, test/eval owners, generators, scripts, agent/model integrations, promotion paths, permissions, concurrency guards, and durable run/ledger evidence. Build a compact map:
SIGNAL -> CURRENT OWNER -> CAPABLE WORKER -> MUTATION SURFACE -> VALIDATION -> INTEGRATION GATE -> NEXT SIGNAL.
If the repository already has an AFK or autonomous mechanism, strengthen or connect it. Do not create a second scheduler, bot, branch writer, test floor, generator, or promotion authority merely because the current mechanism stops too early.

2. FEEDBACK IS A WORK QUEUE, NOT A REPORT ENDPOINT
Ingest concrete signals with provenance: provider run/job/check ID and candidate SHA; failing command/test and first useful error; PR review thread/comment/path/line; static-analysis finding; generated-artifact mismatch; skipped/blocked gate; issue/task identity; runtime receipt; or moved-base/stale-proof evidence. Classify each as ACTIONABLE_REPAIR, TEST_EVOLUTION, PROMOTION_BLOCKED, USER_ONLY, INFORMATION_ONLY, OUT_OF_SCOPE, or SUPERSEDED. Deduplicate already-consumed signal identities so schedules or repeated webhooks do not create churn.

Every ACTIONABLE_REPAIR must become either a concrete repository mutation owned by a capable worker or an exact blocker. A review summary, CI dashboard, comment, issue, artifact, or receipt is evidence for the next pass; it is not itself completion.

3. P07-STYLE NONTERMINAL WORK LOOP
Use this execution invariant:
REFRESH -> INGEST SIGNALS -> SELECT SAFE HIGHEST-VALUE WORK -> EXECUTE -> VALIDATE -> INGEST NEW FEEDBACK -> CRITIQUE -> IMPROVE -> INTEGRATE -> REFRESH -> REPEAT.

A status-only pass is a failed pass when safe agent-capable work exists. Every meaningful pass must mutate owned state, produce stronger decision-relevant evidence, integrate a coherent green slice, or prove the exact blocker that prevents the next safe pass. CI success, an open PR, a review summary, or a scheduled wake-up is not terminal state while an actionable queue item or integration gate remains. The first green result triggers at least one evidence review for new findings instead of granting automatic closure.

4. DISPATCH TO THE CAPABLE OWNER; DO NOT MAKE ONE MEGABOT
Use existing specialized owners rather than teaching this loop to impersonate every subsystem. P07 owns general bounded repository execution and its fixed-point/mainline discipline. P32 owns repair of an established failing CI lane. P112 owns bootstrap of a missing deterministic automated-test floor. P113 owns proactive risk-driven evolution of an already trustworthy floor. P104 owns bounded deterministic repository-native code generation from canonical inputs. P105 owns validation and authorized promotion of an already-authored exact candidate. Route other domain work to its current repository owner, developer, agent, model, script, generator, or workflow.

Dispatch parallel independent lanes when supported, but enforce one writer per mutation surface and serialize shared registries, schemas, generators, lockfiles, workflows, manifests, and default-branch mutation. A worker's completion claim is input evidence; the coordinator still revalidates and integrates the combined result.

5. FEED CI AND REVIEW RESULTS BACK INTO DEVELOPMENT
When CI fails, preserve the exact candidate identity and failing gate, then route the smallest repair to the owner that can change the implicated surface. When a review bot or human leaves a concrete finding, bind the thread/comment identity to the candidate head, validate the finding, repair it when correct, rerun affected proof, and resolve/respond only after current evidence supports the disposition. When a test/eval reveals a product defect, keep or add the regression and repair the product owner; do not stop after proving that the defect exists. When a promotion gate fails, P105 must remain fail-closed while this loop routes the repair; a new exact candidate must re-enter promotion after repair.

Feedback should reach developers, scripts, agents, models, PRs, and any other authorized work conductor in a form they can act on: exact target, owned surface, evidence, acceptance condition, forbidden scope, and command or mutation entrypoint. Do not force the operator to shuttle CI logs or review text between systems when repository/provider automation can preserve that context.

6. AFK WAKEUPS ARE NOT AFK WORK
Push, pull_request, review, issue, workflow_run, repository_dispatch, provider webhook, queue, and justified schedule events are wakeups. A cron tick that merely reruns unchanged checks and posts another summary is not useful AFK development. Prefer event-driven wakeups when the source can emit them; use schedules as bounded recovery/revalidation mechanisms when events are unavailable or stale state must be revisited. Record timing as best-effort when the provider does not guarantee exact scheduling.

On every wakeup, recover durable state from the repository/provider rather than model memory: last consumed signal IDs, current candidate/base, active work items, last proof, unresolved reviews, integration state, budgets, and blockers. If nothing relevant changed and no safe queued work remains, exit cleanly without manufacturing commits.

7. COERCE REAL WORK, NOT STATUS THEATER
If a safe mutation is available, a response that only explains, reports, waits, polls, opens a PR, restates failures, or asks the operator to run ordinary checks violates this prompt. Advance the first executable gate yourself. If an existing AFK workflow, prompt, bot, script, or agent repeatedly stops after producing feedback, repair that mechanism's contract/routing so the next run consumes its own evidence and continues development. Prefer changing the durable system over compensating forever with a smarter one-off agent.

Do not use artificial churn to satisfy the loop. No-op passes are valid only when they prove the fixed-point stop condition or a real blocker. Preserve cost/token/runtime budgets and cap repeated retries on unchanged evidence.

8. SAFETY, AUTHORITY, AND RECURSION
AFK authority does not expand because no human is watching. Preserve branch protection, environment approvals, review requirements, secrets policy, production boundaries, output containment, generated-surface ownership, and user-only gates. Do not grant a model new credentials, approve its own protected deployment, weaken a failing test, force-push, or bypass review to keep the loop moving. Guard bot/workflow commits against recursive self-triggering and conflicting writers. Stop a lane at the protected gate while continuing independent safe lanes.

9. PROVE THE LOOP IN THE REAL PROVIDER
Static orchestration prose is insufficient. Exercise one bounded canary feedback cycle in the actual provider where safe: create/select a controlled failing check, review finding, or stale-proof condition; observe the signal with exact identity; route it to the intended worker; perform the repair; rerun the affected gate; ingest the new result; conduct the second critique/improvement pass; and integrate one coherent green slice when authorized. Prove the operator did not have to relay ordinary logs or manually restart the development logic. Do not leave a deliberate defect in the durable branch.

10. TERMINAL CONDITIONS
Terminal state requires a bounded fixed point: requested acceptance criteria are proven; current feedback/review/test queues contain no unresolved in-scope actionable signal; exact-head validation is current; authorized integration is complete or specifically blocked; post-integration containment is verified; and remaining items are USER_ONLY, OUT_OF_SCOPE, UNSAFE with evidence, or exact blockers. An open PR, green CI, generated report, review-ready label, or successful scheduled run is nonterminal by itself.

After every merge/integration, refresh current default-branch truth and continue remaining queue items from that new floor. Most of the work should happen AFK because the loop carries signal context forward to the next capable worker, not because it runs a timer frequently.

DELIVER
Keep the operator closeout compact: signals consumed; real work passes executed; workers/owners used; files/artifacts changed; CI/review findings repaired; exact-head validation; integrations; remaining blockers/user-only gates; proof ceiling; and whether the loop reached fixed point. Do not substitute an activity report for the repository changes it should describe.

prompts.name: SysAdminSuite Protected-Network Endpoint Probe & Identity Gate
prompts.copy_content:
PROBE MANAGED WINDOWS ENDPOINTS THROUGH SYSADMINSUITE BEFORE MUTATION. DO NOT GUESS FROM STALE INVENTORY, DIRECTORY PRESENCE, OR A SINGLE PING RESULT.

Repo/product: SysAdminSuite or resolve the active SAS repository from context.
Targets: xyz_hostnames_inventory_or_resolve_from_current_work
Requested downstream action: xyz_deploy_repair_printer_directory_config_or_other
Approved network posture: resolve only from current repository/operator evidence; do not embed private network details into reusable public prompt text.

MISSION
Produce a fresh, read-only endpoint reachability and identity gate that tells the next workflow whether a target is safe to act on. This prompt owns recon and classification, not deployment or repair.

1. RESOLVE THE CANONICAL PROBE OWNER
Read the current SAS governance, command surface, preflight/probe implementation, target resolver, evidence paths, and network policy. Use the repository-owned command rather than inventing an ad hoc ping/nslookup script when a canonical probe exists.

2. ESTABLISH NETWORK POSTURE
Confirm the execution host is on an approved path for the target environment using evidence the repository recognizes. If the current network is wrong, classify the result as a network-posture blocker; do not label the endpoint offline and do not mutate DNS, firewall, trust, VPN, routing, or directory state merely to make the probe pass.

3. RESOLVE EACH TARGET
For every requested hostname or inventory record, capture the canonical target identifier, DNS resolution, and the strongest supported read-only reachability checks. Keep these states separate: RESOLVED_AND_REACHABLE, DNS_UNRESOLVED, RESOLVED_UNREACHABLE, STALE_OR_AMBIGUOUS_DIRECTORY_RECORD, IDENTITY_UNCONFIRMED, PERMISSION_BLOCKED, and UNKNOWN. Use repository-native names when they already exist.

4. CONFIRM IDENTITY
When the workflow requires a serial, asset, computer-account, or other identity check, obtain it only from an approved source. Directory existence alone is not fresh device proof. Do not count a target as confirmed when current network or identity evidence is missing.

5. PRESERVE EVIDENCE
Write or reuse the canonical SAS receipt/report path. Record target, timestamp, execution context, resolver result, evidence source, classification, and next owner. Avoid secrets and sensitive excerpts. For batches, emit a rollup without losing per-host evidence.

6. ROUTE, DO NOT MUTATE
A passed endpoint goes to the exact requested downstream owner. A failed endpoint receives only the smallest read-only diagnostic that can resolve its class. Do not install software, change AutoLogon, map printers, move directory objects, reboot, or clean remote state in this prompt.

VALIDATE
Prove the probe is read-only, uses the canonical SAS target/network resolver, preserves UNKNOWN honestly, distinguishes DNS/network/directory/identity failures, and produces fresh per-target evidence.

DELIVER
Report the per-target classification ledger, evidence location, confirmed targets, unresolved/blocked targets, proof ceiling, and the exact next owning workflow for each class.

prompts.name: SysAdminSuite Clinical-Core Deployment with AutoLogon Isolation
prompts.copy_content:
DEPLOY THE SYSADMINSUITE CLINICAL CORE WITHOUT CROSSING INTO AUTOLOGON OR UNRELATED ENDPOINT MUTATION. DO NOT TURN A BASELINE SOFTWARE DEPLOYMENT INTO AN ALL-IN-ONE MACHINE CONFIGURATION SCRIPT.

Repo/product: SysAdminSuite or resolve the active SAS repository from context.
Target: xyz_hostname_or_inventory_record
Clinical-core manifest/package set: resolve from current repository truth.
Excluded follow-up lane: AutoLogon and any other component the current SAS contract separates from the baseline.

MISSION
Install or repair exactly the repository-authorized clinical-core baseline on the intended managed Windows endpoint, with package integrity and per-package evidence, while preserving the explicit boundary that AutoLogon is handled separately.

1. REFRESH THE DEPLOYMENT CONTRACT
Read current SAS governance, target resolver, clinical-core manifest/package registry, deployment wrapper, evidence contract, installed-state reader, and current restart policy. Never rely on an old remembered package list when the repository can resolve the current set.

2. PREFLIGHT BEFORE STAGING
Run the approved protected-network/DNS/identity gate and confirm target eligibility. Prove the required privilege/execution identity at the level the SAS workflow demands. A guest/unapproved network, unresolved target, wrong host, or privilege mismatch is a blocker, not permission to improvise another transport.

3. BASELINE CURRENT STATE
Capture the current installed state for every clinical-core package and the excluded surfaces relevant to non-regression, especially AutoLogon and repository-defined sign-on/badge middleware. Record only the evidence required for comparison; do not expose credentials or private values.

4. STAGE EXACT PAYLOADS
Use the canonical source and staging path. Verify the expected digest, preferably SHA-256 when that is the repository contract, before execution. Do not guess package paths, silently substitute versions, or continue with an unverified payload.

5. DEPLOY ONLY THE CLINICAL CORE
Use the supported SAS wrapper/entrypoint and the required execution context. Execute the exact package set with bounded waits and per-package results. Skip already-compliant items only when the canonical idempotency check proves they are compliant. Do not mutate AutoLogon, sign-on configuration, trust, DNS/firewall policy, or other excluded machine state. Do not reboot unless the current canonical deployment contract explicitly owns and authorizes it.

6. VERIFY AND CLOSE THE BASELINE
Re-read installed state and compare every required package. Produce PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN per package plus target-level status. Prove excluded surfaces remain unchanged. Preserve the canonical receipt/evidence pointer. If a package is partial or unknown, clinical-core closure remains open.

7. HAND OFF THE SEPARATE FINAL STEP
Only after the clinical-core receipt is green may separately requested AutoLogon work route to the AutoLogon-only prompt. Do not start that lane automatically when the user asked only for clinical-core deployment.

DELIVER
Target, current manifest identity, preflight result, package/hash ledger, execution context, per-package result, excluded-surface non-regression proof, evidence path, proof ceiling, and exact next owner.

prompts.name: SysAdminSuite AutoLogon-Only Crash-Safe Recovery
prompts.copy_content:
RECOVER OR COMPLETE AUTOLOGON THROUGH THE DEDICATED SYSADMINSUITE AUTOLOGON-ONLY LANE. DO NOT REDEPLOY THE CLINICAL CORE AND DO NOT BLINDLY RERUN AFTER AN INTERRUPTED OR UNKNOWN-PARTIAL ATTEMPT.

Repo/product: SysAdminSuite or resolve the active SAS repository from context.
Target: xyz_hostname_or_current_target
Prior AutoLogon run/evidence pointer: xyz_receipt_path_or_resolve_from_session_state

MISSION
Make AutoLogon a bounded final-step workflow with crash recovery. Reconstruct what happened, prove what is safe to clean or resume, then execute only the supported AutoLogon path.

1. RECOVER CURRENT TRUTH FIRST
Read SAS governance, the AutoLogon-only wrapper, interrupted-run recovery entrypoint, evidence schema, target resolver, network gate, staging/output-root rules, task/process ownership rules, and restart policy. Prefer persistent session/run state such as the repository's `sas context` / `sas next` seam when available instead of asking the operator to reconstruct a long terminal history manually.

2. RE-PREFLIGHT THE TARGET
Confirm the intended endpoint and approved protected-network posture again. A network change, unresolved hostname, wrong endpoint, privilege mismatch, or stale run pointer invalidates assumptions from the earlier attempt. Do not work around the gate with guessed domains, alternate transports, trust repair, or unrelated system changes.

3. RECONSTRUCT THE INTERRUPTED ATTEMPT
Determine the last proven phase: preflight, S4U/task probe creation, staging, installer entered, installer completed, verification, cleanup, or restart. Inspect current scheduled-task/process/staging state and preserved receipts. UNKNOWN is a real state. Do not infer that installer code ran merely because a wrapper started, and do not infer that it did not run merely because the terminal crashed.

4. BOUND S4U / TASK / PROCESS FAILURES
When a scheduled-task or S4U probe timed out or a native task command hung, identify the exact task and PID ownership before terminating anything. Prove whether the installer phase was entered. Clean only probe/task/staging objects owned by this run and only when the canonical recovery contract allows it. Never kill a process, delete a scheduled task, or erase staging based only on a similar name.

5. RESUME THROUGH THE SUPPORTED ENTRYPOINT
Once prior state is bounded, use the repository-supported AutoLogon-only wrapper/recovery entrypoint and supported evidence/output root. Do not route through a known-broken launcher/menu simply because it is visible. Keep the command short and repeatable for field use; complexity belongs behind the canonical wrapper.

6. VERIFY POST-STATE AND CLEANUP
Verify the intended AutoLogon state using the canonical state reader, confirm required restart behavior only when the workflow owns it, prove temporary state-reader/probe tasks are gone, and preserve the final receipt/run pointer. Do not modify unrelated sign-on middleware or redeploy baseline packages.

7. FAIL CLOSED ON UNKNOWN PARTIAL STATE
If exact ownership, installer-entry state, target identity, or cleanup scope cannot be proven, stop the AutoLogon lane and report the blocker. The correct response is not another deployment attempt.

DELIVER
Target, recovered prior phase, network/preflight result, task/process/staging ownership findings, cleanup performed, AutoLogon execution result, restart result when applicable, residue check, evidence path, proof ceiling, and exact next safe action.

prompts.name: SysAdminSuite Fleet Batch Endpoint Change Orchestrator
prompts.copy_content:
RUN A FLEET-SCALE SYSADMINSUITE ENDPOINT CHANGE WITHOUT TURNING A SINGLE-PC COMMAND INTO A BLIND FOR-EACH LOOP. KEEP THE OPERATION ONE-COMMAND-FIRST, TERMINAL-AGNOSTIC, CRASH-RECOVERABLE, AND EVIDENCE-DRIVEN.

Repo/product: SysAdminSuite or resolve the active SAS repository from context.
Underlying endpoint operation: xyz_canonical_deploy_printer_config_repair_or_other_owner
Target inventory: xyz_csv_json_text_registry_or_current_inventory
Desired batch action: xyz_action

MISSION
Orchestrate one already-bounded SAS endpoint operation across many PCs. This prompt owns inventory resolution, fleet planning, bounded scheduling, persistent progress, retry classification, and rollup. It does not reimplement the underlying mutation logic.

1. RESOLVE THE SINGLE-HOST OWNER FIRST
Identify the canonical SAS command/module that safely performs the requested operation on one endpoint. Read its preflight, idempotency, evidence, cleanup, restart, and forbidden-scope rules. If there is no safe single-host owner yet, stop fleet mutation and build/repair that owner first rather than embedding an ad hoc implementation into the batch layer.

2. NORMALIZE INVENTORY
Accept the repository-supported CSV/JSON/text/registry form. Resolve every target through the canonical hostname/identity resolver. Detect duplicates, blanks, malformed records, conflicting instructions, and unsupported action values before mutation. Produce a resolved plan that the operator or automation can inspect.

3. PREFLIGHT PER HOST
Apply the relevant protected-network/identity and operation-specific read-only checks to every target. Mark each host READY, ALREADY_COMPLIANT, BLOCKED, INVALID, or UNKNOWN using repository-native states when available. Do not let one reachable PC imply that the rest of the batch is reachable.

4. DRY-RUN / CONFIRMATION BOUNDARY
When the SAS operation supports WhatIf/preview or an explicit action confirmation, preserve it. Show target -> operation -> expected state change -> owning command before mutation. Do not bypass a canonical confirmation merely because the batch is large.

5. BOUNDED EXECUTION
Use bounded concurrency chosen by repository policy or a conservative existing default; never spawn unbounded remote jobs. Serialize operations that the underlying owner requires to be serialized. Bound every wait. Record start/end, attempt, result, and evidence pointer per host.

6. IDEMPOTENCY AND RETRIES
Before each mutation, re-read enough current state to avoid repeating already-proven work. Retry only failures classified as transient and only within the repository's bounded retry policy. HARD_FAILURE, UNKNOWN_PARTIAL_STATE, permission, identity, and network-posture failures are not blind-retry candidates.

7. CRASH / TERMINAL RECOVERY
Persist session state continuously enough that a terminal close, shell crash, or workstation restart does not erase which targets completed. Prefer the SAS `context` / `next` / resume seam when present. A resumed run must consume prior receipts and skip targets already proven complete unless their state has materially changed.

8. ROLLUP WITHOUT HIDING HOSTS
Emit totals for success, already-compliant, retryable failure, hard failure, blocked, and unknown, plus exact per-host details/evidence pointers. Overall green is valid only when every required target has an accepted terminal state.

FIELD UX
Expose short repeatable technician commands. Hide orchestration complexity behind repository-owned wrappers; do not make technicians paste long try/catch/finally blocks or edit scripts for each site/package set.

DELIVER
Resolved inventory/plan, execution command, concurrency/retry settings, per-host result ledger, persistent session/evidence path, rollup, unresolved targets, proof ceiling, and exact resume/next command.

prompts.name: SysAdminSuite Reversible Printer Mapping & Audit
prompts.copy_content:
MAP, UNMAP, OR AUDIT WINDOWS PRINTERS THROUGH SYSADMINSUITE AS A REVERSIBLE FIELD WORKFLOW. DO NOT BLINDLY REMAP, FALL BACK TO A DIFFERENT SECURITY/NETWORK MODEL, OR TURN A QUEUE PROBLEM INTO TRUST/DNS/FIREWALL/GPO MUTATION.

Repo/product: SysAdminSuite or resolve the active SAS repository from context.
Targets: xyz_one_or_many_managed_windows_hosts
Printer source: xyz_print_server_and_queue_or_supported_inventory
Requested action: MAP | UNMAP | AUDIT

MISSION
Give technicians a short, repeatable, portable printer workflow that resolves the network and queue first, shows the intended change, performs only the requested machine-wide action, and leaves enough evidence to prove or undo it.

1. USE THE CANONICAL SAS PRINTER OWNER
Read current printer commands/wrappers, target resolver, network gate, state reader, evidence paths, batch schema, and map/unmap implementation. Do not replace repository-owned printer logic with a long local PowerShell snippet merely because it is convenient in the current shell.

2. RESOLVE TARGET + NETWORK + QUEUE
Confirm each endpoint identity and an approved network path to the target and print infrastructure. Resolve the canonical print server/queue rather than guessing from display names. A network mismatch is a distinct blocker; do not call the printer offline merely because the current technician machine cannot reach it.

3. READ CURRENT MACHINE-WIDE STATE
Audit the existing printer/connection/port state at the supported machine-wide level. Record whether the requested queue is absent, already mapped, mapped differently, conflicted by name/port, or unknown. Do not use a per-user fallback when the canonical workflow requires system-wide state.

4. SHOW THE PLAN BEFORE MUTATION
For each target/queue, display current state -> requested action -> expected post-state -> collision decision -> owning command. Preserve canonical WhatIf/preview behavior and explicit MAP/UNMAP confirmation when required. A large batch does not waive confirmation or plan visibility.

5. MAP / UNMAP REVERSIBLY
Use the repository-authorized system-wide mechanism and its paired inverse. MAP must have a state-derived UNMAP/undo path; UNMAP must identify exactly which machine-wide mapping is being removed. Skip already-compliant state only after the canonical reader proves it. Serialize target changes when the SAS implementation requires serialization.

6. DO NOT INVENT NETWORK OR SECURITY FALLBACKS
Do not mutate trust, DNS, firewall, GPO, VPN, routing, or directory policy to make printer mapping work. Do not use direct-IP mapping, per-user mapping, or print-test-page actions when current repository/operator policy forbids them. If a separately authorized canonical owner explicitly permits a different transport, route to that owner rather than silently changing this prompt's contract.

7. VERIFY POST-STATE
Re-read machine-wide printer state and verify the exact queue mapping/removal. Record evidence per target/queue, including collision disposition and undo information. A command exit code without state verification is not closure.

8. BATCH SAFELY
For many PCs and queues, consume the supported batch inventory, preserve a resolved plan, keep per-host/per-queue receipts, and emit a rollup that separates success, already-compliant, blocked, hard failure, and unknown. Do not lose individual failures inside an aggregate green count.

FIELD UX
Prefer clickable/short technician entrypoints with easy server/queue inputs and safe examples sourced from repository docs; do not hard-code private production infrastructure into reusable public prompt text.

DELIVER
Resolved plan, per-target/queue pre-state, action/confirmation, post-state, undo path, evidence pointer, blocked/failing items, batch rollup when relevant, proof ceiling, and exact next safe action.

prompts.name: SysAdminSuite Active Directory Computer OU Move & Verification
prompts.copy_content:
MOVE ACTIVE DIRECTORY COMPUTER OBJECTS THROUGH SYSADMINSUITE WITH AN EXACT OLD-OU -> NEW-OU PLAN AND POST-MOVE VERIFICATION. DO NOT GUESS DISTINGUISHED NAMES OR BUNDLE RENAME, DOMAIN-JOIN, GROUP, GPO, TRUST, OR DNS CHANGES INTO AN OU MOVE.

Repo/product: SysAdminSuite or resolve the active SAS repository from context.
Targets: xyz_one_or_many_computer_names_or_inventory
Destination OU: xyz_operator_requested_ou_name_or_authoritative_identifier

MISSION
Perform the smallest authorized directory mutation: move existing computer objects to one explicitly resolved destination OU and prove the result. Keep the technician surface short; hide directory lookup and verification behind the canonical SAS wrapper when one exists.

1. RESOLVE THE CANONICAL DIRECTORY OWNER
Read current SAS governance, directory/OU command implementation, target resolver, authorization model, evidence schema, and batch conventions. Use the repository-owned wrapper rather than pasting a one-off directory script when the owner exists.

2. LOOK UP SOURCE OBJECTS READ-ONLY
Resolve each requested computer object uniquely. Capture its canonical identity and current distinguished name/OU. Classify NOT_FOUND, DUPLICATE_OR_AMBIGUOUS, DIRECTORY_UNREACHABLE, PERMISSION_BLOCKED, or UNKNOWN separately. Do not create a missing computer object to make the move succeed.

3. RESOLVE THE DESTINATION OU EXACTLY
Resolve the requested OU to its authoritative distinguished name through current directory/repository evidence. A friendly label with multiple matches is ambiguous and blocks mutation. Never guess a DN from naming conventions.

4. SHOW THE MOVE PLAN
Before mutation, emit one line per target: computer -> current OU -> destination OU -> MOVE or ALREADY_CORRECT / BLOCKED. For batches, detect duplicate targets and conflicting destination instructions before changing anything.

5. MOVE ONLY THE COMPUTER OBJECT
Execute the repository-authorized move operation for READY objects. Skip already-correct objects idempotently. Do not rename the object, recreate it, rejoin the endpoint, change groups, modify GPOs, alter trust, change DNS, or perform unrelated cleanup. Do not expose directory credentials or tokens in logs or prompt output.

6. VERIFY FROM DIRECTORY TRUTH
Re-read every attempted computer object after mutation and compare its distinguished name/parent OU to the resolved destination. A successful command exit without a confirming directory read is not closure. Record exact per-object result and evidence pointer.

7. BATCH + RECOVERY
For many computers, keep per-object receipts and a rollup. A repeat/resume run must skip objects already proven in the requested OU and retry only failures the repository classifies as safe/retryable. UNKNOWN partial state requires a fresh directory read before another move.

DELIVER
Resolved destination OU, source-object ledger, old-to-new plan, mutation results, post-move distinguished names, blocked/ambiguous objects, evidence path, proof ceiling, and the exact next safe action for any remainder.

prompts.name: Web Contact Form Semantic Validation & Mutation-Hardened Release Guard
prompts.copy_content:
HARDEN THE WEB CONTACT FORM WITH SEMANTIC VALIDATION, MUTATION FIXTURES, AND BUILT-OUTPUT-GATED RELEASE. DO NOT SHIP A FORM THAT PASSES ONLY ON HAPPY-PATH INPUTS.

Repo: xyz_repo_or_path
Form route/handler: xyz_contact_form_route_or_resolve_from_repo
Stack: xyz_nextjs_react_resend_turnstile_or_resolve_from_repo

MISSION
Make the contact/email form reject bypasses that survive naive string checks. Treat HTML semantics, request-access indirection, console leakage, email-payload forgery, second-sink execution, and build-artifact drift as first-class failure modes. Start from current markup and handler evidence, harden validators with HTML-aware and semantic checks, cover each bypass with a CRLF-stable mutation fixture that can both pass and fail, and bind the whole guard into release:check so a green unit suite cannot hide a stale vulnerable build.

WHERE TO LOOK FIRST
- Form markup: every <input>, <textarea>, <select>, <button> inside <form id="contact-form"> and every external control with form="contact-form"; unnamed controls; native submit vs JS submit; required attribute position/order; disabled/hidden controls.
- Request surfaces: direct req.body access, computed access (req["body"], req[variable], destructured alias), aliased handler arguments, middleware-normalized bodies, and framework helpers that re-expose fields under new names.
- Console surfaces: all console.* calls across app, api, handler, and client code.
- Email payload: Resend (or equivalent) from/to/subject/text/html construction, template interpolation sites, and any concatenation of user fields into payload.
- Turnstile/CAPTCHA: script/widget import, explicit render calls, token verification, and passive resource hints (preload/prefetch/preconnect, CSS/JS resource detection beyond active script execution).
- Tests/fixtures: existing validators, mutation fixtures, built-output directory, and package.json scripts including release:check.
- Built output: what release:check actually executes, whether it rebuilds then validates, and whether it consumes built HTML/JS.

1. SEMANTIC FORM-CONTROL ASSOCIATION
Controls belong to a form by spec, not by proximity.
- A control with form="contact-form" is associated even when outside the <form> element. A control without form attribute and outside the form is not associated.
- Resolve association by HTML semantics: ancestor form chain plus explicit form attribute, not string proximity or file order.
- UseWhen entrypoints: internal text/email/message inputs, external form="contact-form" honeypots or injected fields, and any form-associated custom element.
- Mutations: add/remove an external form="contact-form" control, move a control outside the form without form attribute, change form id without updating form attribute.

2. UNNAMED AND EXTERNAL NATIVE-SUBMIT REJECTION
Unnamed controls and external native submits are bypass vectors.
- Reject any form-associated control that has no name attribute or has empty name, regardless of id/class/placeholder.
- Reject external native submit: <button type="submit" form="contact-form"> or <input type="submit" form="contact-form"> that is not inside the intended form. Programmatic fetch/JS submit owned by the app is separate; native HTML submit that escapes client validation is the defect.
- Required-attribute order handling: treat required as order-insensitive and value-insensitive (required, required="", required="required", required="true" are all required). Do not match required by literal string order or exact required="required" only.

3. COMPUTED AND ALIASED REQUEST ACCESS DEFENSES
Attackers and future refactors use indirection. The guard must too.
- Deny computed access to request fields: req["body"], req[dynamic], req.body[dynamic], (req as any)[field], and destructured aliases (const {body: b}=req). Normalize field access to a single validated extraction path.
- Aliased handler parameters: function handler(reqAlias, res) where reqAlias is later used as reqAlias.body["field"] must be tracked as the same sink.
- Fixtures: one valid direct-access control that must pass, one computed-access bypass that must fail, one aliased-access bypass that must fail.

4. ALL-CONSOLE DENIAL
Do not allow console.* as a logging side-channel for form data or verification tokens.
- Deny all console methods (log, info, warn, error, debug, trace, table) in form, api, handler, and adjacent validation code. No allowlist.
- Fixtures: a console.log(userEmail) fixture that must be rejected, and a validated control without console that must pass.

5. SEMANTIC RESEND PAYLOAD CHECKING
Do not check Resend by string containing "Resend" alone.
- Validate semantic payload shape: the Resend (or email provider) send/create call receives an object whose to/from/subject/text/html fields are not unsanitized concatenation of raw user fields. Use AST or semantic call-site inspection, not substring.
- Reject template-interpolation injection: payload html/text that interpolates ${userInput}, {{userInput}}, {userInput}, or JSX {userInput} without escaping/sanitization. HTML-aware tag boundary: reject payloads that can close a tag or inject a new element because user input is placed inside tag content/attributes without escaping.
- Comment-safe payload location remains a bypass: payload html that places user input inside <!-- userInput --> or other comment contexts must be rejected unless the output context proves comments are not executed. Location inside comments is not safe.
- Fixture pair: one sanitized Resend payload that must pass, one interpolated-into-html payload and one comment-placed payload that must fail.

6. SECOND-SINK MUTATIONS
First-sink guard is necessary but not sufficient.
- After initial validation/sanitization, track second-sink handlers: alternate api route, webhook forward, queue job, email text vs html dual sink, analytics sink, or log sink that re-uses the raw field.
- Add at least one second-sink mutation where the first sink is sanitized but the second re-uses the raw user field and must be rejected.

7. CRLF-NORMALIZED MUTATION FIXTURES
Windows checkout line endings must not mask failures.
- Normalize fixture input and expected output with CRLF handling: the same logical payload must assert identically under \r\n and \n. Run fixtures or normalize line endings before comparison so a test that passes on Unix but fails on Windows is a defect, not a flaky environment.
- Provide at least: one CRLF-normalized mutation fixture (CRLF and LF variants prove same verdict), one semantic form-control fixture (external form="contact-form" included, outside-without-form excluded), one unnamed/external-submit rejection fixture, and one required-attribute-order-agnostic fixture.

8. HTML-AWARE TAG BOUNDARIES, COMMENT-SAFE LOCATION, TEMPLATE-INTERPOLATION, AND PASSIVE TURNSTILE-RESOURCE DETECTION (0a7a4c4… HARDENING)
This is the HTML-aware boundary set.
